facts.big: If I had more time, I’d practise more
facts.label: Segundo condicional
facts.sub: If + passado simples, would + verbo. Use para situações irreais ou improváveis. Para conselhos: If I were you, I’d… (sempre were).

facts.label: Se + passado, faria
facts.sub: Use if + passado simples na primeira parte e would + verbo na segunda: If I had more time, I’d practise more. Fala de algo irreal ou improvável agora. Não use would depois de if.

facts.label: Se eu fosse você…
facts.sub: Para dar conselho, use If I were you, I’d + verbo: If I were you, I’d wake up earlier. Com I, we usam were, não was. É uma forma educada de sugerir algo.

compare.ask: If I had more time, I’d practise more.
compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “se eu tivesse mais tempo, eu praticaria mais”.
compare.tip: Diga: “If I had more time, I’d practise more.”
compare.us: Em inglês é parecido: If I had more time, I’d practise more. Use o passado simples depois de if e would + verbo na outra parte. Para conselho: If I were you, I’d…

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.
group: Leia as duas colunas e peça que apontem a maior diferença.

pages.title: A café patio in Austin · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a warm evening in Austin. Paulo works all day in an office. His daily routine is very busy. He studies English late at night. Alma meets him at a small table outside. She has a few ideas about his schedule.
“Paulo, you look tired. Do you study at night?” says Alma. “Yes, after work. If I had more time, I’d practise more.” says Paulo. “If I were you, I’d wake up earlier and study before work.” says Alma.
